comment_rover_id: rover_id is per-rover and lives in the untracked picar-cfg.local.json (created by install.sh) so it survives git pulls. Defaults to 1 if that file is absent.
comment_fleetManagerUrl: 'auto' = discover the Fleet Manager on the LAN (OS-agnostic, no IP/hostname needed). Or set an explicit http://host:port. Empty disables.
comment_telemetry: Battery/power come from the flight controller (SYS_STATUS, POWER_STATUS). batteryWarnLevel is a remaining-percentage threshold; batteryWarnVolts is a voltage threshold that always works regardless of where the percentage comes from. batteryWarnVolts is set to 6.8 V, which is 3.4 V/cell on the fleet's 2S packs — a warn level, not a cutoff. It was null until 2026-08-04, and because ArduPilot reports battery_remaining=0 on this fleet the percentage branch never fired either, so NO state of charge could raise a warning at all: a 2S pack at 3.0 V total rendered clean and set no fleet status bit. Change this for a different cell count.
comment_battery_no_reading: batteryWarnOnNoReading makes an unreadable battery monitor a WARNING rather than an all-clear. SYS_STATUS maps both 0 mV and 65535 mV to unknown, so without this a dead pack or a failed power module reported no trouble while 1% remaining did. Set false only on a vehicle with no battery monitor at all.
comment_battery_pct: The flight controller's own battery percentage is only usable when it coulomb-counts, which needs BATT_MONITOR and BATT_CAPACITY set AND current_consumed actually reported. On rover3 it is NOT: BATT_CAPACITY=3300 and BATT_MONITOR=4 are set, yet 24169 BATTERY_STATUS frames carried current_consumed=-1 (not measured) and battery_remaining=0. So set battery_empty_volts/battery_full_volts for your pack and the percentage is interpolated linearly from voltage instead. Both must be set, finite, and full > empty, or the estimate stays off. Examples: 2S LiPo 6.0/8.4, 3S LiPo 9.0/12.6, 6-cell NiMH 6.0/8.4. Telemetry reports which source it used in battery.pctSource ('flightcontroller' or 'voltage'); a voltage estimate SAGS UNDER LOAD, so it is smoothed over battery_pct_median_samples readings and the UI marks it with a leading ~.
comment1: pigpion is for the native picpio lib in C
comment2: mavproxy is backend for mavproxy to talk w/ pixhawk, push pwm there
comment_mavproxy_radio: mavproxy_radio_system: sysId of the SiK telemetry radio, if one is fitted. RADIO_STATUS is exempt from the autopilot target-system gate because SiK emits source system 51 (ASCII 3), not the autopilot sysId. null accepts any source, which is a hole bounded by radio telemetry being display-only - set this once the fitted radio sysId is known.
comment_mavproxy_overlay: The param overlay is reasserted until read-back confirms every critical parameter, because a TCP connection to MAVProxy does not prove its serial master is usable and the first attempt can be lost entirely.
comment_drivetrain: drivetrain_settle_ms: delay between the neutral+DISARM of a gear/diff change and actually moving the actuator, so a coasting vehicle slows first. Not a confirmed stop - this vehicle has no wheel encoder and GPS is disabled.
comment_light: Light module on Pixhawk output 6, driven by RC channel 6 passthrough (SERVO6_FUNCTION=1). On/off only, not dimmable. Its own endpoint pair so the module can be trimmed without touching the motion channels PWM range. The light is NOT reset by a fail-safe: an operator who has just lost control wants the vehicle to stay visible.
comment_webrtc_load: OFFERED LOAD IS DELIBERATELY LOW. MediaMTX's rpicamera source does not act on WebRTC congestion feedback, so the encoder holds this bitrate however bad the link gets, and lowering it is the only lever picar has. 80 kbps is a FALSIFICATION TEST set on 2026-08-06, not a tuned value. A drive that day froze at 100 ft with 200 kbps: the controller correctly stepped down at -67 dBm, MediaMTX discarded 20-25 frames/s for 14 s, and CONTROL failed roughly 30 s BEFORE video did - six 'no input for 1000 ms' fail-safe trips while video was still flowing. The link's nominal tx rate was 72 Mbit/s at -47 dBm, so 200 kbps was never a bandwidth problem, which means video load may not be the binding constraint at all. Dropping to 80 kbps decides it: if control still trips at the same distance, video is exonerated and the answer is RF or the control transport, not the encoder. If it holds, airtime contention was real. RESTORE to 200 once that question is answered - 80 kbps at 320x240@10 is deliberately poor. idr_period 10 is one IDR per second, which bounds how long a frozen picture stays frozen; on UDP one lost packet destroys its whole frame and a keyframe spans several, so frequent IDRs are what make recovery possible.
comment_webrtc_max_readers: maxReaders caps concurrent viewers of the camera path. It is 1 because a SECOND viewer doubles what the rover must transmit over the same half-duplex airtime the control channel needs, and it is invisible to the operator - measured on 2026-08-06, an agent's forgotten browser tab streamed video through the middle of a range test from a tunnelled address, logging 'reader is too slow, discarding ~42 frames' every second while the operator was out at distance. A capped path refuses the second reader instead of quietly halving everyone's link.
comment_adaptive_bitrate: video_adaptive_apply selects HOW an adaptive rung is enforced, and 'observe' is the default because the cheap mechanism DOES NOT WORK. Measured on rover3 2026-08-06: writing a new rpiCameraBitrate into mediamtx.yml makes MediaMTX log 'reloading configuration (file changed)' and NOT recreate the rpiCamera source - the mtxrpicam child kept the same PID at 14 s, 20 s and 40 s after the write while the file plainly held the new value, so the encoder never saw it. 'observe' therefore decides rungs and LOGS them without applying anything, which is not a placeholder: the dBm thresholds have never been fitted to a real drive, and an observe run produces exactly that data at zero cost to the operator's video. Set 'restart' to actually enforce rungs via a mediamtx restart - that is proven to work because the UI video-params path already does it, but each step DROPS THE WEBRTC SESSION and the browser must renegotiate, on a degrading link, which is when it fires. Choose it deliberately. video_adaptive_bitrate: false disables the whole thing.
comment_latency: Video latency is bounded by DROPPING stale frames rather than queueing them. h264_drop_delta_bytes: per-client WebSocket backlog above which delta frames are dropped (keyframes still sent so the client can resync). h264_drop_all_bytes: hard backlog above which everything is dropped. mjpeg_drop_bytes: socket backlog above which an MJPEG frame is skipped.
